svg.title: Claude asks whether the task list builds the design in an acceptable order, with the options Approved and Changes needed; the author picks Approved, and the switch-task skill ends the turn with the switch message: the session holds about 149000 tokens, a /compact line that says what was finished, what comes next and what to keep, then /ponderly:implement-spec switch-task-eval-gaps to run, and a line that the compaction can be skipped.

g.text: ponderly — start-task
⏺ AskUserQuestion(questions: [{"question": "Do the tasks in
.ponderly/specs/switch-task-eval-gaps/tasks.md build the design in an order you accept? Put
anything missing or wrong in the free text.", "header": "Approve", "multiSelect": false,
"options": [{"label": "Approved", "description": "The seven tasks and their four waves are right;
hand off to implement-spec."}, {"label": "Changes needed", "description": "Something is missing
or wrong; say what in the free text."}]}])
Your questions have been answered: "Do the tasks in
.ponderly/specs/switch-task-eval-gaps/tasks.md build the design in an order you accept? Put
anything missing or wrong in the free text."="Approved". You can now continue with these answers
in mind.
⏺ Skill(skill: ponderly:switch-task, args: /ponderly:implement-spec switch-task-eval-gaps)
● This task is done and the next one is a different task. This session holds about 149000 tokens.
Compact first, so the next task does not re-read this one on every turn:
/compact We just finished the spec for the switch-task eval gaps. Next we build it wave by wave
with implement-spec, which reads .ponderly/specs/switch-task-eval-gaps/. Keep that the branch is
switch-task-eval-gaps at main 0c059db with the three spec files uncommitted, that no paid eval
case runs without the author's yes, task 5.1 included, and that the switch-task skill, the hooks
and the merged compact-at-task-switch spec are not changed. Drop the detail of the finished work.
Then run:
/ponderly:implement-spec switch-task-eval-gaps
You can skip the compaction and run the next step as it is.
